scope: The spec query full-text retrieval command. Belongs here: FTS5 MATCH semantics; rank-ascending results; superseded exclusion; --limit bounds. Does not belong here: file→requirement resolution (→ RSLV). Boundary case: a bare AND OR FTS5 grammar error is a QURY usage-error (exit 2) contract.

requirements.statement: spec query answers full-text retrieval over requirement text and rationale via FTS5.
requirements.why: Rung-1 agent retrieval — a semantic-ish hit a plain grep for the id would miss.

requirements.statement: spec query matches porter-stemmed forms of the search text, so querying 'renewal charge' returns a requirement whose text says 'renews'.
requirements.why: Without stemming, agents must guess the author's exact wording; the headline find-the-requirement-by-the-value-moment retrieval promise silently fails.

requirements.statement: spec query returns TERM-domain glossary definitions in a Terms group beside requirement hits, discriminated by the FtsHit key so a term hit is distinguishable from a requirement hit, while terms stay excluded from the coverage matrix
requirements.why: the glossary becomes searchable at query time — the only-allowed-jargon payoff of §4.11 is visible where an author is already looking, without leaking terms into coverage obligations

requirements.statement: When searching requirements, spec query shall exclude deprecated requirements from the results.
requirements.why: Dead guidance surfacing as live sends an agent to build against a promise that no longer holds.

requirements.statement: When given search text, spec query shall return matching requirements ranked best-match first, bounded by --limit (default 10, maximum 1000).
requirements.why: An agent acts on the top hits; unranked or unbounded output turns retrieval into scrolling, and the wrong requirement gets built against.

requirements.statement: When searching requirements, spec query shall exclude superseded requirements from the results.
requirements.why: A superseded statement surfacing as live sends an agent to build against a contract that no longer holds.

requirements.statement: When the search text and a requirement's wording differ only by word inflection, spec query shall still match — stemming makes 'renewal charge' return a requirement whose text says 'renews'.
requirements.why: Without stemming, agents must guess the author's exact wording, and retrieval silently fails on everyday inflection differences.

requirements.statement: When a spec query match is a TERM-domain glossary definition, the spec CLI shall return it in a Terms group beside the requirement hits, discriminated by the key field so a term hit is distinguishable from a requirement hit.
requirements.why: A term hit rendered as an undistinguished requirement row reads as a coverage obligation, and the payoff of searchable jargon is lost exactly where an author is already looking.

requirements.statement: When the search text and a requirement's wording differ only by word inflection, spec query shall still match — 'renewal charge' shall return a requirement whose text says 'renews'.
requirements.why: When retrieval demands the author's exact wording, everyday inflection differences silently return nothing and duplicates get minted for requirements that already exist.
